theme.title: Splash season
theme.subtitle: Golden State, 2015–16
theme.recap: The Warriors won their first 24, reached the All-Star break at 48–4, never lost at home for more than a year and made threes at a rate nobody had seen.

questions.prompt: The 2015–16 Warriors opened the season with how many straight wins?
questions.note: 24 in a row before their first loss.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Warriors began the 2015–16 season by winning their first 24 games,

funFacts.text: Assistant Luke Walton coached Golden State's opening stretch while Steve Kerr recovered from back surgery.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Warriors opened the regular season on October 27 with assistant coach Luke Walton coaching

funFacts.text: Milwaukee finally ended the opening streak, with the Bucks handing Golden State its first loss.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The winning streak to start the season ended at 24 games when they were beaten by the Milwaukee Bucks

funFacts.text: Draymond Green produced a rare five-by-five stat line in the double-overtime win at Boston.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: During this game Draymond Green recorded a five-by-five game

questions.prompt: What was the Warriors' win total at the 2016 All-Star break?
questions.context: Golden State Warriors · 2015–16 · first half of the season
questions.note: 48–4, the best record ever at the break.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Golden State reached the NBA All-Star break at 48–4, the best start to an NBA season at this juncture.

funFacts.text: Klay Thompson beat teammate Stephen Curry in the All-Star weekend Three-Point Contest.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Klay Thompson won the Three-Point Contest at the All-Star weekend, beating Stephen Curry

funFacts.text: Draymond Green had already tied Tom Gola's Warriors record for triple-doubles in one season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Green tied Hall of Famer Tom Gola's franchise record of nine triple-doubles

funFacts.text: Golden State reached fifty wins faster than any NBA team before it had done.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: fastest team to reach 50 wins in a season, accomplishing this in just 55 games

questions.prompt: Golden State set an NBA record for consecutive regular-season home wins. How long was the streak?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The Warriors also set an NBA record 54-straight regular-season home-game winning streak,

funFacts.text: The home winning streak stretched across two seasons, beginning in January 2015.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: which spanned from January 31, 2015, to March 29, 2016

funFacts.text: Boston ended Golden State's long run at Oracle Arena with a narrow April road win.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Golden State lost at home for the first time since January 27, 2015. They fell to the Boston Celtics

funFacts.text: Before Golden State broke it, Chicago's 1990s dynasty had held the home-win-streak record.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: The previous record of 44 was held by the 1995–96 Chicago Bulls

questions.prompt: How many three-pointers did the 2015–16 Warriors make in the regular season?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: They also became the first team to make over 1,000 three-pointers in the regular-season with 1,077,

funFacts.text: Stephen Curry personally contributed 402 made threes during the same regular season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Curry broke his own NBA record for made three-pointers in a season of 286, finishing with 402

funFacts.text: Golden State also led the league in assists per game and offensive rating that season.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: led the league in scoring (114.9 points), field goal percentage (.487), three-point percentage (.416), assists (28.9)

funFacts.text: The Warriors crossed the team thousand-three mark in a game against Portland.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: first team in NBA history to score 1,000 three-pointers in a single season during their 136–111 win against

questions.prompt: On May 9, 2016, Stephen Curry set an NBA record for points in an overtime period. How many did he score?

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: He scored 17 of his points in overtime, which broke the NBA record of 16

funFacts.text: Curry returned from an MCL injury absence to score forty points against Portland.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Curry scored 40 points in his first game back after being out injured for 15 days with an MCL sprain

funFacts.text: The previous overtime-period scoring mark belonged to Gilbert Arenas.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: broke the NBA record of 16 held by Gilbert Arenas for most points scored in an overtime period

funFacts.text: The following day, Curry became the NBA's first unanimous regular-season MVP.

source.name: Wikipedia contributors (CC BY-SA 4.0)
source.quote: Curry is the 11th player to win back-to-back MVP honors and is the first unanimous winner
